title: scheduler probing rate-limiter and hysteresis rework to prevent kernel-selection oscillation
creator: Evan Chu
description:
Summary: During a recent capacity surge the scheduler's exploratory kernel-probing heuristic amplified kernel-selection churn. That churn caused repeated KV-cache misses, increased per-request CPU/GPU context switches, and amplified p95/p99 tail latency for several hosted customers. This ticket implements immediate containment (rate-limits and hysteresis) plus a medium-term safety design to prevent probe amplification during bursty multi-tenant traffic.

Problem details: The scheduler issues aggressive short-lived probe runs to evaluate alternate kernel variants when it detects degraded latency on the primary path. Under sustained surge (concurrent requests peaking > 3x baseline), probes increased in frequency and led to frequent kernel handoffs. Each handoff invalidated warmed KV cache entries and triggered JIT/kernels reloads on the device, producing a cascade: more probes -> more cache churn -> higher latency -> more probes. Existing backoffs were linear and per-request, not per-device or per-queue, so they failed to dampen at scale.

Goals: 1) Stop probe-amplification loops under surge; 2) Preserve safe short-term probing that helps optimize steady-state throughput; 3) Add observability to measure probe amplification; 4) Provide rollout plan with feature-flagged canary and automated rollback.

Proposed solution (short-term containment):
- Add a per-device exponential backoff on exploratory probing with configurable cap (device_probe_backoff_base_ms and device_probe_backoff_max_ms).
- Introduce a per-device token-bucket rate limiter for probe attempts (default 1 probe per 5s per device, burst=2).
- Add a hysteresis metric to kernel affinity calculation: require affinity delta > hysteresis_threshold for N consecutive requests before switching kernels (configurable).
- Circuit-breaker: if kernel_switches_per_minute > threshold, disable exploratory probes for that device for cooldown_window.
- Force fallback path that preserves warmed KV cache (prefer kernel variants marked as "cache-compatible") when cooling probes are disabled.

Proposed solution (medium-term hardening):
- Move probing decisions to a device-global coordinator that can see device-level success/failure signals and enforce collective backoffs (avoid per-request conflicting signals).
- Improve kernel metadata to include compatibility labels (cache-compatible, quant-safe, attention-optimized) so scheduler can prefer cache-compatible variants during high churn.
- Add synthetic repro bench that simulates multi-tenant surge with mixed sequence lengths and attention patterns to validate heuristics.

Observability additions (required):
- New metrics: kernel_probe_attempts, kernel_probe_rate_per_device, kernel_switches_per_request, kernel_switches_per_minute, probe_success_rate, cache_eviction_rate_due_to_switch.
- Dashboards/alerts: alert when kernel_switches_per_minute > 5 on any device AND p95 latency increases > 20% vs baseline.

Testing and rollout:
- Unit tests for token-bucket/backoff logic and hysteresis.
- Integration test with synthetic bench to surface probe amplification patterns.
- Canary rollout via feature flag to 1% of devices for 48h, then 10%/24h, 50%/48h with automated rollback if kernel_switches_per_minute or p99 latency regresses beyond thresholds.

Artifacts and links: Confluence design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/pages/runtime-probing-2026, repro notebook (internal GDrive): https://drive.redwood.ai/surge-probe-repro, initial PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/2861 (WIP), dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/ABCD/kernel-probe-amplification, incident writeup: https://incidents.redwood.ai/2026-02-kernel-probe-surge

Minimal roll-forward fallback: If the containment changes harm steady-state throughput in canary, we will revert rate limits to relaxed defaults and instead tune hysteresis and affinity thresholds before enabling the full per-device backoff.
comments: 2026-03-02 - Evan Chu: Initial triage: reproduced amplification locally with the synthetic surge bench. Captured timeline and device-level probe logs. Linked incident writeup above. Marking this P1 due to broad customer tail-latency impact.

2026-03-04 - Priya Menon: Implemented local token-bucket PoC and ran bench. Observed 60% reduction in kernel_switches_per_minute and 18% improvement in p95 under the synthetic surge. Pushing a WIP PR to share telemetry. PR link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/2861

2026-03-06 - Marco Ruiz (review): Concern — token-bucket default may reduce beneficial probing that discovers a better kernel for specific attention patterns. Recommend adding a short grace window after node restart where we allow limited probing to warm metrics. Also suggested per-model overrides in config.

2026-03-07 - Priya Menon: Addressed Marco's feedback: added 'grace_probe_quota' for 30s after device/worker start and per-model override via model_probe_policy. Updated PR with unit tests for grace quota behavior.

2026-03-09 - Security/Compliance note (Anika Rao): No secret exposure in metrics. Ensure the dashboard access is restricted to infra+eng roles. Marking security_review_required=false here but will include in enterprise release notes.

2026-03-10 - SRE (Daniel Kim): Added alert thresholds to staging Grafana. Observed no regressions in steady-state workloads for the canary cohort. Requesting canary rollout plan details before prod enablement.
